Okay, here's a template for giving feedback to your manager after conducting an offline B2B sales attempt to a small business that turned out to be a branch, and you received contact information for the head office.  I've included different options for tone and information, so you can tailor it to your specific situation and company culture:

**Subject: Feedback - [Your Name] - Offline Sales Visit - [Date] - [Business Name]**

**Body:**

**Option 1:  Straightforward and Concise** (Good for efficiency and if your manager prefers direct communication)

> Hi [Manager's Name],
>
> Following up on my sales visit today to [Business Name] at [Location if applicable] for [briefly describe the product/service you were offering].
>
> The location I visited is a branch.  I spoke with [Name and Title if you got it], who informed me that decisions are made at the head office.  I was provided with the following contact information for the head office:  [Email Address(es)/Phone Number/Contact Name if provided].
>
> I plan to [Your next steps, e.g., "send an introductory email to the head office contact" or "follow up with a phone call next week"].
>
> Please let me know if you have any suggestions or if you'd like me to approach this differently.
>
> Thanks,
> [Your Name]

**Option 2:  More Detail and Proactive Planning** (Suitable if you want to demonstrate initiative and analysis)

> Hi [Manager's Name],
>
> I wanted to provide feedback following my offline sales visit today to [Business Name] at [Location if applicable] regarding [briefly describe the product/service].  I focused on [mention the original sales objective, e.g. "explaining the benefits of our XYZ service to a local business"].
>
> Upon visiting, I learned that this location is a branch office.  I was able to speak with [Name and Title if you got it],  and they clarified that all purchasing decisions are made at the head office. They provided the following contact information [Email Address(es)/Phone Number/Contact Name] for [Head Office, Department if stated] at the head office.
>
> **My Plan:**
> *   I will [Action 1: e.g., "Draft a personalized email introducing our company and the benefits of [product/service] to the head office contact"]
> *   I will [Action 2: e.g., "Follow up with a phone call next week to check if they have received the email and to discuss their requirements"].
> *   I will [Action 3: e.g. "Try to discover their current supplier]
>
> **Questions/Considerations:**
> *   Are we already targeting this head office? (Check internal CRM)
> *   Do we have any pre-existing relationship or knowledge about the head office?
> *   Would you like me to note the contact info into our CRM or any other internal database?
>
> Please let me know if you have any objections, suggestions, or if you prefer a different approach.
>
> Thanks,
> [Your Name]

**Option 3:  Learning and Optimization Focus** (Emphasizes learning from the experience, Good for a more collaborative environment, or after multiple visits of this type)

> Hi [Manager's Name],
>
> I'd like to share an update from my offline sales visit today to [Business Name] located at [Location if applicable] where I introduced our [product/service].
>
> This particular location is a branch of [Business Name] and purchases are done only at head office level. I spoke with [Name and Title if you got it], and received contact information for [Head Office, Department if stated] at the head office: [Email Address(es)/Phone Number/Contact Name].
>
> **Observations/Reflections:**
> *   The format of the business [if location is open (opening hours), size of the office, style of business etc.].
> *   This experience highlighted to me [Lessons Learned: e.g. "the importance of verifying the business structure before visits," "the need to have head office contact information readily available," etc.].
> *   (Optional) _ I also noticed [Observation about the branch; e.g. "They seemed to be using competitors'  products, with [detail of the competitor if any]."]
>
> **Next Steps:**
> *   I will [Action 1: e.g., "send an introductory email to the head office contact"]
> *  I'll add the head office contact information to the CRM when I have the time.
>
> **Suggestions/Requests** (Optional):
> *   [e.g., "Perhaps we could have a process or tool to quickly identify branches vs. headquarters during the research phase."]
>
> Please let me know your thoughts and if there is anything else I should be doing.
>
> Thanks,
> [Your Name]

**Key Elements to Customize:**

*   **[Manager's Name]:**  Your manager's name.
*   **[Your Name]:**  Your name.
*   **[Date]:**  The date of the visit.
*   **[Business Name]:**  The name of the business you visited.
*   **[Location if applicable]:**  The address or specific branch location.
*   **[briefly describe the product/service you were offering]:**  A sentence or two summarizing what you were selling.
*   **[Name and Title if you got it]:**  The name and title of the person you spoke with at the branch (if you got it).
*   **[Email Address(es)/Phone Number/Contact Name if provided]:**  The contact information for the head office.  Be accurate!
*   **[Your next steps]:**  What you plan to do next (e.g., email the head office, call them, etc.). Be specific.
*   **CRM (Customer Relationship Management) -** make sure you document any new information, contacts and next steps in your organisation's CRM on a daily basis.

**Tips for Writing Your Feedback:**

*   **Be Prompt:** Send the email soon after your visit while the details are fresh in your mind.
*   **Be Clear and Concise:**  Get to the point quickly, without unnecessary jargon.
*   **Be Professional:** Maintain a professional tone throughout.
*   **Focus on the Facts:**  Stick to what happened, what you learned, and your planned actions.
*   **Be Proactive:**  Show that you are taking initiative and thinking ahead.
*   **Proofread:**  Always proofread your email before sending it.
*   **Tailor to Your Company Culture:**  Consider your company's communication style and adjust the tone accordingly.
*   **Adapt based on Feedback:** If your manager provides feedback, incorporate it in future reports.

Good luck with your sales efforts!
